mutants.description: A cache created with capacity=1 is rejected, so single-entry caches cannot be constructed at all.
The hit counter starts at 1 instead of 0, so every cache reports one hit it never served.
len(cache) reports one entry more than the cache actually holds.
Reading a key marks it as the oldest entry instead of the newest, so hot entries are evicted first.
Every cache miss counts the miss counter backwards, so miss statistics go negative.
A cache filled exactly to capacity evicts an entry it should have kept, losing data one insert early.
Overwriting an existing key no longer refreshes its recency, so recently-updated entries are evicted as stale.
Invalidating a key leaves it in the cache with a None value, so the slot still counts against capacity and hit statistics.
Prefix invalidation also removes keys that merely contain the prefix in the middle, deleting unrelated entries.
mutants.search_block: doomed = [key for key in self._data if key.startswith(prefix)]
mutants.replace_block: doomed = [key for key in self._data if prefix in key]

mutants.description: The count returned by invalidate_prefix is one less than the number of entries actually removed.
The last page claims a next page exists, so UIs render a 'next' button that leads to an empty page.
The first page claims a previous page exists, so UIs render a 'previous' button that goes nowhere.
Page counts round down instead of up, so the final partially-filled page is dropped and trailing items become unreachable.
per_page=0 no longer raises a clear error and instead blows up with a raw ZeroDivisionError.
Page.total reports the number of items on the current page instead of the whole collection, breaking any 'showing X of Y' display.
Requesting per_page=1 is rejected as invalid, so single-item pages cannot be served.
mutants.search_block:
if per_page < 1:
        raise ValueError("per_page must be >= 1")
mutants.replace_block:
if per_page < 2:
        raise ValueError("per_page must be >= 1")

mutants.description: Durations written with uppercase units like '1H30M' are rejected instead of parsed.
A trailing number without a unit like '1h30' is silently treated as seconds instead of raising an error.
mutants.search_block:
if number:
        raise ValueError("trailing number without a unit: %r" % text)

mutants.description: Values that themselves contain '=' like 'query=a=b' now crash the parser instead of being kept intact.
Values keep their surrounding whitespace, so 'a= 1 ' parses to ' 1 ' instead of '1'.
Passing percent=None now means a 100% discount instead of no discount, so items are given away free.
A 100% discount is rejected as out of range, so 'make it free' promotions cannot be applied.
The maximum-discount cap works as a floor: small discounts are inflated up to the cap instead of being limited by it.
Runs of spaces are no longer collapsed and tabs or newlines are left untouched, so messy input stays messy.
Text that is exactly `limit` characters long gets needlessly cut and suffixed instead of being returned unchanged.
When the limit is shorter than the suffix, the result exceeds the limit instead of fitting inside it.
Truncated text comes out one character shorter than the limit allows, clipping a character that would have fit.
